correctness.rationale: Each signed transitive A4 action is classified by a conjugacy class of stabilizer and sign character. A4 has exactly seven such types, yielding degrees (1,3,3,4,6,6,12) and centralizer factors (2,6,2,2,4,4,24). The kernel/core calculation makes exactly types 2–6 faithful; Aut(A4) preserves each type, so the normalizer is 24 times the complete centralizer. Orbit-stabilizer and exact rational generating functions then follow. Root-of-unity pole orders prove degree six, period exactly twelve and the leading coefficient. Standalone verification checks profiles and exact arithmetic through n=12, actual subgroup generator counts through n=6 and conjugacy orbits through n=4. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The specific profile-by-profile normalizer theorem, faithful seven-orbit classification, conjugacy-class rational generating function and exact least period are not stated or directly implied by the inspected Coxeter involution and wreath single-element conjugacy work. Schlage-Puchta (2011) covers general homomorphism counts (and can yield the embedded-count EGF after specialization), not subgroup normalizer spectra; this difference is central. Müller (2000) provides a serious potential older general-coverage risk, disclosed below. Originality is relative to accessible scientific comparisons, not a guarantee of priority.
residual_risks: Older wreath-product representation literature, in particular Müller (2000), might contain the same subgroup profile/normalizer specialization; its original full text was not inspected.
A semigroup- or embedding-theoretic reformulation of the same seven-profile table may be unindexed.

General homomorphism-count machinery already implies the enumerator of labeled homomorphisms and, on specialization, the embedded-total exponential generating function; this is explicitly not claimed as a new general method.

value.rationale: The natural nonabelian tetrahedral subgroup problem is solved simultaneously for all ranks of a fundamental Coxeter family, including a complete orbit-type classification, every subgroup normalizer, exact class counts, and a period-12 growth invariant. The distinguishable signed 3-point actions and Aut(A4) lifting create substantive subgroup structural content beyond a generic homomorphism counting substitution. Not claimed to generalize the established wreath-product enumeration machinery.
